channel.title: The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (occrp.org)

item.title: Norway Charges PetroNor Subsidiary, Two Citizens Over Alleged Congo Oil Bribes
item.description: Norway charges two citizens and a PetroNor subsidiary in cross-border “grand corruption” case involving tens of millions in alleged bribes to Congo’s president and his family.

item.title: American Women Who Fled Fiji’s Grace Road Cult Ready to Return to Give Evidence
item.description: An American woman who escaped a Korean doomsday cult in Fiji alleged in a police complaint that she gave free spa treatments to politicians, including the former prime minister.

item.title: Europol: Drug Traffickers Pivot to Smaller Ports as Security Tightens at Europe’s Major Hubs
item.description: Cocaine trafficking into Europe is reaching record levels as criminal networks shift away from major hubs like Antwerp and Rotterdam toward smaller docks and high-tech tactics, including custom-built submarines.

item.title: Repressive States Misuse Interpol Red Notices to Pursue Political Targets: Report
item.description: Russia tops the list of countries issuing Interpol Red Notices, according to a report by Disclose and BBC. Interpol imposed heightened scrutiny on Russian Red Notice requests after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: China Executes 11 in Myanmar-Linked Telecom Fraud Gang
item.description: China Executes 11 in Myanmar-Linked Telecom Fraud Gang

item.title: German Prosecutors Raid Deutsche Bank in Money Laundering Probe
item.description: German prosecutors searched Deutsche Bank offices in Frankfurt and Berlin as part of a probe into suspected money laundering linked to past transactions, adding to a series of high-profile investigations involving the lender.

item.title: Georgia Moves to Tighten Control Over Foreign-Funded NGOs and Media
item.description: Proposed amendments would require government approval for most foreign funding and impose criminal penalties, raising fears of a crackdown on independent civil society and journalism.

item.title: Montenegro Shaken as Convicted Crime Boss Vanishes After Sentencing
item.description: Montenegro’s president has accused the government of systemic failure after Miloš Medenica, the son of a former Supreme Court president, vanished despite being under house arrest following a major organised crime conviction.

item.title: Nigerian Pension Reformer Bought US and UAE Properties Before Money Laundering Conviction
item.description: Authorities seized at least 20 properties in Nigeria after former pension fund official Abdulrasheed Maina was convicted of money laundering. Reporters have now discovered four additional properties, purchased with “cash in hand.”

item.title: Episode 2: Carmelo, Where Are You?
item.description: With reporting from Miami to Madrid, Venezuelan journalist Laura Weffer unpacks the mechanics of the corrupt loan schemes that allowed elites to siphon off $1.2 billion from Venezuela’s state oil company.
